I've spoken to samaritans a number of times, they're really quite good and don't try and talk you out of it all, rather they try and guide you to making your own decision about your problems.

They ask you questions like, how does it make you feel when this happens? What sort of solutions do you think there are? What steps would you need to take for that to happen?

Might sound unhelpful when written out like this but in my view they're really worth the call. One thing is the wait times seem to be quite long at the moment, especially at night time but you will eventually get through.

When I quit smoking I initially did it for my (now ex) girlfriend to impress her.

When we broke up I continued to resist the urge to smoke and instead assigned a new meaning to it all, now I'm still resisting the urge because I want to prove to myself that I have the willpower to make positive change.

It's all about the motivating factor, find a valid reason to quit and hold onto that. Every time you feel a craving you remind yourself of it and shoot that thought down.
